question_text: A 26-year-old African-American woman comes to the physician because of a 4-day history of a nonproductive cough and chest pain. The pain is sharp and worse when she breathes deeply. During this time, she has also had two episodes of hematuria. Over the past 6 months, she has had intermittent pain, stiffness, and swelling in her fingers and left knee. She had two miscarriages at age 22 and 24. Her only medication is minocycline for acne vulgaris. Her temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 138/85 mm Hg. Physical examination shows an erythematous rash on her face. There is mild tenderness over the metacarpophalangeal joints bilaterally with no warmth or erythema. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

                    ### Question
                    A 26-year-old African-American woman comes to the physician because of a 4-day history of a nonproductive cough and chest pain. The pain is sharp and worse when she breathes deeply. During this time, she has also had two episodes of hematuria. Over the past 6 months, she has had intermittent pain, stiffness, and swelling in her fingers and left knee. She had two miscarriages at age 22 and 24. Her only medication is minocycline for acne vulgaris. Her temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F), pulse is 75/min, and blood pressure is 138/85 mm Hg. Physical examination shows an erythematous rash on her face. There is mild tenderness over the metacarpophalangeal joints bilaterally with no warmth or erythema. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

                    ### Options

opb. Low serum levels of C3 and C4
opc. Erosions of the metacarpophalangeal joints
opd. Bilateral enlargement of the hilar lymph nodes

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's symptoms including nonproductive cough, sharp chest pain, erythematous facial rash, joint symptoms, and hematuria, along with a history of miscarriages, suggest systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Expected laboratory findings of low serum levels of C3 and C4, which are typical in SLE due to complement consumption, support this diagnosis. The evidence linking lupus with complement components and the clinical presentation consistent with SLE, rather than drug-induced lupus or other conditions, guide the diagnosis and management.
